sentences.en: Sixty days the papacy had given Martin Luther to recant, or else be damned as a heretic.
sentences.zh: 教皇给了马丁·路德六十天时间悔改，否则就将以异端罪论处。

sentences.en: Now, on the 10th of December, the time was up.
sentences.zh: 现在，到了12月10日，期限已满。

sentences.en: That morning at nine o'clock, Luther walked through one of the three town gates to where a carrion pit lay.
sentences.zh: 那天早上九点，路德穿过三座城门之一，来到了一个腐尸坑旁。

sentences.en: A large crowd had gathered there.
sentences.zh: 一大群人聚集在那里。

sentences.en: One of Luther's colleagues from the university, a theologian named Johann Agricola, lit a fire.
sentences.zh: 路德的一位大学同事，一位名叫约翰·阿格里科拉的神学家，点燃了一堆火。

sentences.en: The spot was where the clothes of those who had died in the nearby hospital were burned, but Agricola, rather than rags, used books as fuel.
sentences.zh: 这个地方原本是焚烧附近医院死者衣物的地方，但阿格里科拉用的燃料不是破布，而是书籍。

sentences.en: All that morning he and Luther had been ransacking libraries for collections of canon lore.
sentences.zh: 那天整个上午，他和路德一直在搜刮图书馆里的教会法典藏书。

sentences.en: Had the two men been able to find a volume of
sentences.zh: 如果这两人能找到一本

sentences.en: Aquinas, they would have burned that as well.
sentences.zh: 阿奎那的著作，他们也会把它烧掉。

sentences.en: Their kindling, though, proved sufficient.
sentences.zh: 不过，他们的引火物已经足够了。

sentences.en: The fire began to blaze.
sentences.zh: 火势开始熊熊燃烧。

sentences.en: Agricola continued to feed books into the flames.
sentences.zh: 阿格里科拉不断地把书投入火中。

sentences.en: Then Luther stepped out from the crowd.
sentences.zh: 这时，路德从人群中走了出来。

sentences.en: He was trembling.
sentences.zh: 他在颤抖。

sentences.en: He held up the papal decree that had condemned his teachings.
sentences.zh: 他举起那份谴责他教义的教皇敕令。

sentences.en: Because you have confounded the truth of God, he said in a ringing voice.
sentences.zh: 他用洪亮的声音说道，因为你们混淆了上帝的真理。

sentences.en: Today, the Lord confounds you into the fire with you.
sentences.zh: 今天，主也要让你们混淆，随你们一起下火狱吧。

sentences.en: He dropped the decree into the flames.
sentences.zh: 他把敕令扔进了火里。

sentences.en: The parchment blackened and curled and turned to smoke.
sentences.zh: 羊皮纸变黑、卷曲，化作了烟雾。

sentences.en: As Luther turned and walked back through the city gate, ashes skittered and swirled on the winter breeze." So that was Dan Brown.
sentences.zh: 当路德转身走回城门时，灰烬在冬日的微风中飞舞盘旋。以上就是丹·布朗的描述。

sentences.en: That was Tom Holland.
sentences.zh: 那是汤姆·霍兰的描述。

sentences.en: So rude.
sentences.zh: 太粗鲁了。

sentences.en: In Dominion, which is your magisterial book about the history of
sentences.zh: 在《主宰》一书中，这是你那本关于

sentences.en: Christianity and how it has shaped the Western world, indeed the entire world, Tom, I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 基督教历史及其如何塑造西方世界，乃至整个世界的权威著作，汤姆，我觉得这样说很公允。

sentences.en: And this is an amazing set piece moment.
sentences.zh: 这是一个令人惊叹的标志性时刻。

sentences.en: So we are now in episode three of this series about the human being who in the last five to 600 years has arguably shaped the Western world as much as
sentences.zh: 我们现在进入了本系列的第三集，讲述的是在过去五到六百年里，可以说塑造了西方世界的人，

sentences.en: any other, maybe more than any other, Martin Luther.
sentences.zh: 甚至比任何人都塑造得更多，他就是马丁·路德。

sentences.en: He is burning a papal bull, a papal decree that was targeted at him.
sentences.zh: 他正在焚烧一份教皇诏书，一份针对他的教皇敕令。

sentences.en: So this is open war with the papacy, Tom.
sentences.zh: 所以这是与教皇的公开战争，汤姆。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So this is ex-Sergé Domine, rise up, O Lord.
sentences.zh: 这就是《起立，主啊》（Exsurge Domine）。

sentences.en: And the Pope had issued it on the 15th of June,
sentences.zh: 教皇于6月15日发布了这份诏书，

sentences.en: 1520 and had given Luther 60 days to recant or be excommunicated.
sentences.zh: 1520年，并给了路德60天时间悔改，否则将被逐出教会。

sentences.en: And the 60 days are up and Luther's response to this deadline is as written in that magisterial prose.
sentences.zh: 现在60天期限已满，路德对这一最后通牒的回应，正如那段权威的文字所写的那样。

sentences.en: And the bull is specifically censoring 41 propositions that Luther has put forward.
sentences.zh: 这份诏书专门审查了路德提出的41条主张。

sentences.en: And one of those propositions, Dominic, is that it's wrong to burn heretics.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，其中一条主张就是焚烧异端是错误的。

sentences.en: And so the danger of death, the fact that Luther by directly taking on the papacy like this, you know, I mean, it's an exceedingly dangerous thing to do.
sentences.zh: 所以死亡的威胁，路德通过这种方式直接挑战教皇，你知道，我的意思是，这是一件极其危险的事情。

sentences.en: This is life and death.
sentences.zh: 这是生死攸关的事。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is happening in Wittenberg, the capital of Frederick, the elector of Saxony.
sentences.zh: 这一切发生在维滕贝格，萨克森选帝侯腓特烈的首府。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Luther is a professor at the university.
sentences.zh: 路德是大学的一名教授。

sentences.en: So Frederick has every stake in kind of backing him.
sentences.zh: 所以腓特烈有充分的理由支持他。

sentences.en: And three years have passed since that great and celebrated act of defiance that we ended episode two with.
sentences.zh: 距离我们在第二集结尾提到的那次伟大而著名的反抗行动已经过去了三年。

sentences.en: Hammering the theses or not on the walls of the church or churches.
sentences.zh: 不管有没有把《九十五条论纲》钉在教堂或教堂的墙上。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Onto the doors of the church.
sentences.zh: 钉在教堂的门上。

sentences.en: And in those three years, Luther has precipitated a crisis on a scale that Latin Christendom has never witnessed before, at least not since the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 在那三年里，路德引发了一场拉丁基督教世界从未见过的规模的危机，至少自11世纪以来从未有过。

sentences.en: Crikey.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And the features of the crisis, they're kind of threefold, really.
sentences.zh: 这场危机的特征，其实可以分为三个方面。

sentences.en: So it's about the church essentially asserting its authority, the medieval church, the Roman church, whatever you want to call it.
sentences.zh: 这本质上是关于教会维护其权威，中世纪教会，罗马教会，无论你怎么称呼它。

sentences.en: So back in 1517, the whole reason why these indulgences are being issued is because the church
sentences.zh: 回到1517年，发行赎罪券的全部原因是因为教会

sentences.en: is manifesting its assumption that Christians can earn their way out of purgatory through buying them or, you know, or through a whole host doing good works, pilgrimages, whatever.
sentences.zh: 正在表现出一种假设，即基督徒可以通过购买赎罪券，或者通过做各种善事、朝圣等等，来赚取脱离炼狱的机会。

sentences.en: This idea that there is a kind of spiritual capital that Christians can draw on to get themselves out of purgatory and get to heaven sooner.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，基督徒可以利用某种“精神资本”来让自己早日脱离炼狱，进入天堂。

sentences.en: And of course, in 1520, the assumption is that the church has the right to eradicate heresy.
sentences.zh: 当然，在1520年，人们认为教会拥有铲除异端的权利。

sentences.en: This is why the Pope has issued the bull.
sentences.zh: 这就是教皇发布诏书的原因。

sentences.en: Can I ask a quick question, Tom?
sentences.zh: 我可以问个简单的问题吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: Lots of people will be thinking this.
sentences.zh: 很多人都会这么想。

sentences.en: Why is it called a bull?
sentences.zh: 为什么它被称为“公牛”（bull）？

sentences.en: It's called a bull, which is obviously a papal bull.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“bull”，显然是指教皇诏书（papal bull）。

sentences.en: That sounds, that's very Protestant.
sentences.zh: 听起来，这非常新教。

sentences.en: But a bull, it's a bull.
sentences.zh: 但“bull”就是“bull”。

sentences.en: It's a kind of a seal that stamps the text of it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种盖在文本上的印章。

sentences.en: Okay, fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧，明白了。

sentences.en: I've always wondered.
sentences.zh: 我一直很好奇。

sentences.en: And, you know, and the church has been doing this for a long time.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，教会长期以来一直这样做。

sentences.en: So one of the phrases that is used in this papal bull that's targeting Luther is the same phrase that people who listen to our episode on the Albigensian Crusades may remember.
sentences.zh: 所以，这份针对路德的教皇诏书中使用的短语，与听过我们关于阿尔比派十字军那一集节目的听众可能记得的短语是一样的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The phrase about the little foxes seeking to destroy the vineyard.
sentences.zh: 关于“小狐狸试图摧毁葡萄园”的短语。

sentences.en: Exactly the same phrase.
sentences.zh: 完全一样的短语。

sentences.en: And Tom, just to remind people, Luther hammered up these theses or nailed them up or didn't, depending on your view, because he was outraged because a bloke was going around,
sentences.zh: 汤姆，提醒一下大家，路德把这些论纲钉上去，或者没钉上去，取决于你的看法，是因为他很愤怒，因为有个家伙到处走，

sentences.en: a kind of carnivalesque monk was going around selling indulgences to raise money for the rebuilding of St. Peter's Basilica in Rome.
sentences.zh: 一个像狂欢节一样的僧侣到处兜售赎罪券，为重建罗马圣彼得大教堂筹集资金。

sentences.en: And Luther just thought this was disgraceful.
sentences.zh: 路德认为这简直是丢人现眼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it turns out to be even worse because actually loads of the money is going to a bank that has given money to an underage bishop who wanted to become archbishop.
sentences.zh: 结果更糟糕，因为实际上大量的钱流向了一家银行，而这家银行给了一个未成年主教贷款，让他得以成为大主教。

sentences.en: So it's all fabulously corrupt.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都极其腐败。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's one aspect of it.
sentences.zh: 所以这是其中的一个方面。

sentences.en: The church basically trying to put the lid on this kind of bubbling rebellion.
sentences.zh: 教会基本上试图压制这种正在酝酿的叛乱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And the second thread, of course, is Luther defying really fundamental teachings of the church.
sentences.zh: 当然，第二条线索是路德挑战了教会真正根本的教义。

sentences.en: So in 1517, when he's attacking indulgences, he is also attacking the entire dogma that sinners can
sentences.zh: 所以1517年，当他攻击赎罪券时，他也在攻击整个教条，即罪人可以

sentences.en: basically earn their way out of purgatory, that sinners have agency in getting rid of the penalty for their own sins.
sentences.zh: 基本上通过自己的努力脱离炼狱，罪人有能力消除自己罪孽的惩罚。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that then leads him on to question the leading role claimed by the papacy and indeed actually the entire clergy.
sentences.zh: 这随后引导他质疑教皇乃至整个神职人员所声称的领导地位。

sentences.en: So he's starting to move towards a position that the clergy have no particular status.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始倾向于一种立场，即神职人员没有任何特殊的地位。

sentences.en: And so much of this comes from Luther saying he's been the professor of Bible studies at the university in Wittenberg.
sentences.zh: 而这一切很大程度上源于路德说他一直是维滕贝格大学的圣经研究教授。

sentences.en: And so much of this is him saying, actually, do you know what?
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为他在说，其实，你知道吗？

sentences.en: None of this is in the Bible.
sentences.zh: 这些在圣经里根本找不到。

sentences.en: And if everything is meant to come from the Bible, this is all just tosh that has been dreamed up subsequently.
sentences.zh: 如果一切都应该来自圣经，那么这些都是后来编造出来的废话。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so it's partly from his reading of the Bible and it's partly from his tugging on a thread and the whole carpet falls to pieces.
sentences.zh: 所以这部分源于他对圣经的解读，也部分源于他拉动了一根线，结果整块地毯都散架了。

sentences.en: So if you question a fundamental dogma, then you start to question the role of the papacy, then you start to question the role of the clergy.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你质疑一个基本教条，那么你就会开始质疑教皇的角色，然后你就会开始质疑神职人员的角色。

sentences.en: And essentially, Luther is coming to a much more democratic understanding of what it is to be a Christian, one in which the division between
sentences.zh: 本质上，路德正在形成一种更民主的基督教理解，在这种理解中，

sentences.en: the clergy and the laity is being erased.
sentences.zh: 神职人员和平信徒之间的鸿沟正在被抹去。

sentences.en: So, you know, he says every true Christian, whether living or dead, has a part in all the blessings of Christ and the church.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他说每一个真正的基督徒，无论生死，都在基督和教会的所有祝福中占有一席之地。

sentences.en: Is he thinking he's getting back to the early Christians?
sentences.zh: 他是在想回归早期基督徒吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like the Acts of the Apostles kind of Christians?
sentences.zh: 像《使徒行传》那样的基督徒？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so he's starting to construct an understanding of Christian history, which is radically opposed to the traditional one.
sentences.zh: 所以他开始构建一种与传统基督教历史截然不同的理解。

sentences.en: So he is essentially saying that you have the early church and then it all goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 他本质上是在说，早期教会是好的，然后一切都变坏了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he is moving towards a position in which the papacy is the whore of Babylon, as described in the book of Revelation.
sentences.zh: 他正走向一种立场，即教皇是《启示录》中所描述的“巴比伦大淫妇”。

sentences.en: And therefore, you know, a thousand years and more, it's been corrupting and polluting the pure teachings of Christ, which is obviously a very radical revision.
sentences.zh: 因此，你知道，一千多年来，它一直在腐蚀和污染基督的纯粹教义，这显然是一个非常激进的修正。

sentences.en: It's not going to go down well with the Pope.
sentences.zh: 教皇肯定不会高兴的。

sentences.en: No, it's not going to go down well, as we see, because he issues his bull.
sentences.zh: 不，正如我们所见，他不会高兴，所以他发布了诏书。

sentences.en: But the third aspect of what is making this a crisis is that Luther is an absolute master of self-promotion.
sentences.zh: 但导致这场危机的第三个方面是，路德是一个绝对的自我推销大师。

sentences.en: And, you know, this is really unexpected.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这真的很出人意料。

sentences.en: I mean, he's a professor in an obscure university, but he just kind of lights the touch paper.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他只是一所默默无闻大学的教授，但他就像点燃了导火索。

sentences.en: And his mastery of particularly of printing, which we talked about in the previous episode, I mean, printing has been around for
sentences.zh: 他对印刷术的掌握，我们上一集谈到过，我的意思是，印刷术已经存在了

sentences.en: about a century, but he turns out to be absolutely suited to a kind of social media revolution.
sentences.zh: 大约一个世纪了，但他证明自己非常适合某种社交媒体革命。

sentences.en: I mean, so Alec Ryrie, the great historian of Protestantism, he says he turns out to have a kind of raw Trumpian brilliance at German language polemic.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，伟大的新教历史学家亚历克·里里说，他在德语论战方面展现出了一种原始的、特朗普式的才华。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, people have been buying printed matter, but Luther makes it exciting.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你知道，人们一直在购买印刷品，但路德让它变得令人兴奋。

sentences.en: And so they get into the habit of buying it and perhaps kind of reading it out to people who can't read and so on.
sentences.zh: 于是他们养成了购买的习惯，也许还会读给那些不识字的人听，等等。

sentences.en: And so it's Luther really who generates the market for buying printed matter in a way that no one had done previously.
sentences.zh: 所以确实是路德创造了购买印刷品的市场，这是以前从未有人做过的。

sentences.en: And you know, your Trumpian analogy, there's a kind of populist side to Luther's rhetoric, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且你知道，你那个特朗普式的类比，路德的修辞里确实有一种民粹主义色彩，不是吗？

sentences.en: He's brilliant at describing things in very aggressive, scatological, sometimes funny,
sentences.zh: 他非常擅长用极其激进、粗俗、有时很有趣、

sentences.en: raw, kind of earthy terms in a way that maybe virtually no other theologians can do.
sentences.zh: 原始、接地气的词汇来描述事物，这是几乎没有其他神学家能做到的。

sentences.en: So he can reach people who other people can't reach?
sentences.zh: 所以他能接触到别人接触不到的人？

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对可以。

sentences.en: And the other thing that he does is that he's very, very good at staging a public event.
sentences.zh: 他做的另一件事是，他非常、非常擅长策划公共活动。

sentences.en: So the burning of the bull in 1520, it's a deliberately dramatic thing.
sentences.zh: 所以1520年焚烧诏书，这是一件刻意戏剧化的事情。

sentences.en: This is not what heretics do.
sentences.zh: 异端分子通常不会这样做。

sentences.en: Heretics who are condemned kind of, you know, they hide.
sentences.zh: 被谴责的异端分子通常会躲起来。

sentences.en: They don't publicly defy the
sentences.zh: 他们不会公开反抗

sentences.en: Pope because that would be mad.
sentences.zh: 教皇，因为那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But Luther can do it because he has, Frederick is kind of guarding his back.
sentences.zh: 但路德能做到，因为他有腓特烈在背后撑腰。

sentences.en: But you know, he's staging a kind of festival of defiance.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，他是在策划一场反抗的节日。

sentences.en: And in the wake of the burning of the bull, he has got all his students behind him.
sentences.zh: 在焚烧诏书之后，他得到了所有学生的支持。

sentences.en: So the students are rallying to him.
sentences.zh: 所以学生们都团结在他周围。

sentences.en: So the day after the burning of the bull in Wittenberg, students build an enormous float and they, they kind of festoon it with parodies of papal bulls and decrees and so on.
sentences.zh: 在维滕贝格焚烧诏书的第二天，学生们制作了一个巨大的花车，他们用教皇诏书和法令的模仿品装饰它，等等。

sentences.en: And they drive it around the town and then they burn the whole lot.
sentences.zh: 他们把它开遍全城，然后把所有东西都烧了。

sentences.en: And one of them has dressed up as a Pope in a kind of, you know, the papal tiara, and he then tosses his tiara into the fire.
sentences.zh: 其中一个人打扮成教皇，戴着教皇三重冠，然后他把三重冠扔进了火里。

sentences.en: So this is a kind of great festival of defiance and it's fun.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场伟大的反抗节日，而且很有趣。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So why are people doing that?
sentences.zh: 那么人们为什么要那样做呢？

sentences.en: Because what Luther is saying is very scandalous.
sentences.zh: 因为路德所说的话非常令人震惊。

sentences.en: So there are two possibilities there that either the students
sentences.zh: 这里有两种可能性，要么是学生们

sentences.en: kind of are converted to Luther's way of thinking, maybe because he's such a brilliant teacher, or maybe because there was always a latent audience for that message.
sentences.zh: 被路德的思想所折服，也许是因为他是一位出色的老师，或者也许是因为那个信息一直存在潜在的受众。

sentences.en: Or are they just doing it because it's fun?
sentences.zh: 还是他们只是觉得好玩？

sentences.en: I think both.
sentences.zh: 我认为两者都有。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: And I think that, I mean, I guess we are so prone to not thinking that statements on Christian doctrine are exciting.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，我的意思是，我想我们太容易认为关于基督教教义的声明是不令人兴奋的了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, it's not the kind of thing that, that enthuses people by and large today, but back then it is the most thrilling thing you can do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这在今天并不是那种能让人热血沸腾的事情，但在当时，这是你能做的最令人激动的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I mean, you just have to look at the sense of excitement that powers, I don't know, the pushing of doctrines that are offensive to conservatives today, say on social media.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你只需要看看那种推动力背后的兴奋感，我不知道，比如在社交媒体上推动那些让保守派感到冒犯的教义。

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: I mean, people love it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们很喜欢这样。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And likewise, conservatives quite enjoy kind of punching back.
sentences.zh: 同样地，保守派也很享受这种反击的感觉。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Do you know what I was thinking about?
sentences.zh: 你知道我在想什么吗？

sentences.en: I was thinking about 2020, the surge in people like attacking statues and stuff after the death of George Floyd.
sentences.zh: 我在想2020年，乔治·弗洛伊德去世后，人们掀起的那股攻击雕像之类的浪潮。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，正是如此。

sentences.en: Some people are there because they really believe in the cause.
sentences.zh: 有些人参与其中是因为他们真的信仰某种事业。

sentences.en: Some people are there because it's a laugh.
sentences.zh: 有些人参与其中只是为了找乐子。

sentences.en: They want to get out, the carnivalesque side of protest, the intoxication of it.
sentences.zh: 他们想走出去，享受抗议活动中那种狂欢的一面，那种令人陶醉的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think that that is exactly right because in the long run, statues will be toppled, icons will be toppled in due course.
sentences.zh: 我认为这说得非常对，因为从长远来看，雕像终会被推倒，偶像也终会被推翻。

sentences.en: And for reasons that are exactly analogous to the toppling of statues of slavers or whatever, that they are seen to be sinful.
sentences.zh: 而且原因与推倒奴隶主雕像之类的情况完全类似，因为它们被视为是有罪的。

sentences.en: And a public display of your godliness is as exciting in the 21st century as it was in the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 在21世纪，公开展示你的虔诚，就像在16世纪一样令人兴奋。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So it all goes back to Luther basically.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切基本上都要追溯到路德。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So today I think we should look at how we get from
sentences.zh: 所以今天我认为我们应该看看他是如何从

sentences.en: Luther banging up the theses, if that's what he does, to him being excommunicated.
sentences.zh: 路德贴出《九十五条论纲》（如果那是他所做的事），一直到他被逐出教会的过程。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And what happens in the wake of the 95 theses going up is that he has them printed in German as well as
sentences.zh: 《九十五条论纲》发布后发生的事情是，他让人把它们印成了德文版，当然还有

sentences.en: Latin.
sentences.zh: 拉丁文版。

sentences.en: And these start to hit the bookstalls in the new year of 1518.
sentences.zh: 这些论纲在1518年新年开始出现在书摊上。

sentences.en: And they are produced by presses across the entire empire.
sentences.zh: 它们由整个帝国各地的印刷厂印制。

sentences.en: So the whole of what is now Germany and indeed Switzerland and in what will be the Netherlands as well.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在的整个德国，当然还有瑞士，以及未来的荷兰地区。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And because the theses are sharp, they're understandable, they're often quite witty, people can understand them.
sentences.zh: 因为这些论纲言辞犀利、通俗易懂，而且往往非常风趣，人们都能看懂。

sentences.en: And they kind of really enjoy reading up.
sentences.zh: 他们读起来确实非常过瘾。

sentences.en: It kind of gives them a frisson, you know, almost a kind of the shiver of blasphemy about them.
sentences.zh: 这给他们带来了一种战栗感，你知道，几乎是一种亵渎带来的快感。

sentences.en: And to remind people an important point, the empire is a very strange fragmented patchwork.
sentences.zh: 提醒大家一个重要点，当时的帝国是一个非常奇怪且支离破碎的拼凑体。

sentences.en: So the imperial authority to deal with this necessarily is limited and depends upon local rulers, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以处理此事的帝国权威必然有限，且依赖于地方统治者，不是吗？

sentences.en: And that will be really important in Luther's story.
sentences.zh: 这对路德的故事来说非常重要。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in particular, the emperor is quite ill.
sentences.zh: 特别是当时皇帝病得很重。

sentences.en: And that means very likely if there's going to be an imperial election very soon.
sentences.zh: 这意味着很可能会很快进行帝国选举。

sentences.en: And that of course gives an enormous power to Frederick,
sentences.zh: 而这当然给了腓特烈巨大的权力，

sentences.en: Frederick, Luther's protector.
sentences.zh: 腓特烈，路德的保护者。

sentences.en: It's one of only seven electors.
sentences.zh: 他是仅有的七位选帝侯之一。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: But even so, the church has no option but to respond to Luther's challenge.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，教会除了回应路德的挑战外别无选择。

sentences.en: And this is partly because it seems that the sale of indulgences really starts to fall off in the wake of Luther's attack.
sentences.zh: 这部分是因为在路德的攻击下，赎罪券的销售额似乎真的开始下降了。

sentences.en: But it's also because Luther has sent a copy to Albrecht, the Archbishop of Mainz, who is the guy basically who's caused the whole problem.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为路德给美因茨大主教阿尔布雷希特寄了一份副本，而他基本上就是造成整个问题的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Extraordinary that he sent it to the very person.
sentences.zh: 竟然寄给当事人，真是不可思议。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's like someone tagging you into a social media thing, exposing you or something, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像有人在社交媒体上艾特你，曝光你之类的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And so Albrecht then sends it to Rome to get a kind of ruling in the center of things.
sentences.zh: 于是阿尔布雷希特把它寄到了罗马，想在权力中心寻求一个裁决。

sentences.en: And the tradition is that the pope doesn't recognize that it's a crisis at all.
sentences.zh: 而当时的传统是，教皇根本没意识到这是一场危机。

sentences.en: He just thinks it's a load of monks squabbling.
sentences.zh: 他只觉得这不过是一群僧侣在吵架。

sentences.en: And it's kind of the lordly tone of a politician in 2010 turning his nose up at Twitter, saying it doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 这就像2010年的政客用那种傲慢的语气对推特嗤之以鼻，说那根本不重要。

sentences.en: It's unimportant.
sentences.zh: 那无关紧要。

sentences.en: Nothing on this matters.
sentences.zh: 这些事一点都不重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Well, back in Germany, they definitely have a sense of crisis.
sentences.zh: 好吧，回到德国，他们确实有一种危机感。

sentences.en: So the Dominicans give Tetzel, the guy who's been flogging the indulgences, an honorary doctorate so that he can take on Luther as an equal.
sentences.zh: 多米尼加修会给了特策尔——那个一直在兜售赎罪券的家伙——一个荣誉博士学位，这样他就能以平等的身份对抗路德。

sentences.en: Because of course, Luther has a doctorate.
sentences.zh: 因为路德当然拥有博士学位。

sentences.en: He's a doctor.
sentences.zh: 他是一位博士。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Tetzel is boasting that within three weeks of getting his doctorate, he will have Luther in the flames.
sentences.zh: 特策尔吹嘘说，拿到博士学位后的三周内，他就会把路德送上火刑架。

sentences.en: And there's no question Luther is in danger.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，路德处于危险之中。

sentences.en: But because he has the backing of Frederick, basically he's safe.
sentences.zh: 但因为他有腓特烈的支持，基本上他是安全的。

sentences.en: And he also has the backing of, you know, we talked about the students, the students are already rallying behind him.
sentences.zh: 而且他还有支持，你知道，我们之前提到的学生们，学生们已经开始支持他了。

sentences.en: They get hold of Tetzel's repudiation of Luther and burn it.
sentences.zh: 他们拿到了特策尔反驳路德的文章，并将其烧毁。

sentences.en: So this is happening very, very early on.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切发生得非常非常早。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that book burning will be a feature of the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，焚书将成为宗教改革的一个特征。

sentences.en: It actually begins with the reformers.
sentences.zh: 实际上正是从改革者开始的。

sentences.en: It's not the papacy that is the first to burn books.
sentences.zh: 并不是教廷最先开始焚书的。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is interesting.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那确实很有趣。

sentences.en: And it's interesting that it's students burning books.
sentences.zh: 而且有趣的是，焚书的是学生们。

sentences.en: I mean, remember when we did the Nazi series and we talked about how Nazi book burnings are driven by students and their lecturers, not by people against the students' wishes?
sentences.zh: 我是说，还记得我们做纳粹系列节目时，谈到纳粹焚书是由学生和他们的讲师推动的，而不是违背学生意愿的人吗？

sentences.en: Well, and again, I mean, I think that you just have to look at the world today to realize that students quite enjoy, if not burning books, then having them banned.
sentences.zh: 嗯，再说一次，我认为你只需要看看今天的世界，就会意识到学生们相当享受这种行为，即使不是焚书，也是禁书。

sentences.en: Yeah, did they do?
sentences.zh: 是吗，他们真的这么做吗？

sentences.en: You know, there is a kind of, you know, an excitement in it, tearing down traditional structures and so on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这其中有一种快感，推倒传统结构等等。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And he also has the backing of growing numbers of the faculty in Wittenberg.
sentences.zh: 而且他还得到了维滕贝格大学越来越多的教职员工的支持。

sentences.en: So two particular will play key roles in his story.
sentences.zh: 其中有两人在他的故事中扮演了关键角色。

sentences.en: So one is the professor of theology who's also the chancellor of the university.
sentences.zh: 一位是神学教授，同时也是大学校长。

sentences.en: He's a guy called Andreas von Karlstadt.
sentences.zh: 他叫安德烈亚斯·冯·卡尔施塔特。
zh_words: 安德烈亚斯·冯·卡尔施塔特

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And he had actually given Luther his doctorate, even though he's actually three years younger than Luther.
sentences.zh: 尽管他实际上比路德小三岁，但他确实授予了路德博士学位。

sentences.en: And there's a much younger scholar who's the professor of Greek, Philip Melanchthon, who's only 21.
sentences.zh: 还有一位更年轻的学者，希腊语教授菲利普·梅兰希通，他当时只有21岁。

sentences.en: So quite Enoch Powell.
sentences.zh: 挺像伊诺克·鲍威尔的。

sentences.en: He is like Enoch Powell.
sentences.zh: 他就像伊诺克·鲍威尔。

sentences.en: Does he speak like Enoch Powell?
sentences.zh: 他说话像伊诺克·鲍威尔吗？

sentences.en: Are you going to do him in your Birmingham accent?
sentences.zh: 你要用你的伯明翰口音来模仿他吗？

sentences.en: No, I'm not.
sentences.zh: 不，我不会。

sentences.en: I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我不会。

sentences.en: He'd renamed himself.
sentences.zh: 他给自己改了名。

sentences.en: He did.
sentences.zh: 他确实改了。

sentences.en: His name is actually Schwarzert, which means black earth and black earth has been translated into Greek.
sentences.zh: 他的原名其实是施瓦策特（Schwarzert），意思是“黑土”，而“黑土”被翻译成了希腊语。

sentences.en: And this is very much the kind of jape that professors at Wittenberg like to get up to.
sentences.zh: 这非常像维滕贝格的教授们喜欢搞的那种恶作剧。

sentences.en: Does that count as a jape?
sentences.zh: 那也算恶作剧吗？

sentences.en: Is that not just a terrible affectation?
sentences.zh: 那难道不是一种糟糕的矫揉造作吗？

sentences.en: So Luther does it as well.
sentences.zh: 所以路德也这么做了。

sentences.en: So Luther's name is actually Luda.
sentences.zh: 路德的原名其实是路达（Luda）。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But he thinks this isn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得这名字不够好。

sentences.en: So he calls himself Eleutherius, which in Greek means the freed one.
sentences.zh: 所以他称自己为“Eleutherius”，在希腊语中意为“被释放者”。

sentences.en: Oh, come on.
sentences.zh: 噢，得了吧。

sentences.en: And he then makes more accessible as Luther.
sentences.zh: 然后他把它简化成了路德（Luther）。

sentences.en: I think less of him now, Tom, knowing that.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，知道这些后，我对他的评价降低了。

sentences.en: So Luther also is a kind of, it's a classicist's joke.
sentences.zh: 所以路德这也是一种古典学者的笑话。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Great banter.
sentences.zh: 很棒的玩笑。

sentences.en: Great banter.
sentences.zh: 很棒的玩笑。

sentences.en: But Luther is making a serious point because he's saying he's freed, the freed one.
sentences.zh: 但路德是在表达一个严肃的观点，因为他说他是被释放者，获得自由的人。

sentences.en: So what exactly has he been freed from?
sentences.zh: 那么他到底从什么中获得了自由？

sentences.en: So he thinks presumably he's been freed from superstition, obscurantism, error, the darkness of not knowing the love of God.
sentences.zh: 他大概认为自己从迷信、蒙昧主义、错误，以及不知上帝之爱的黑暗中获得了自由。

sentences.en: Is that it basically?
sentences.zh: 基本上就是这样吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So he gets summoned to a chapter meeting of the Augustinians.
sentences.zh: 1518年4月，他被传唤参加奥古斯丁修会的会议。

sentences.en: He's an Augustinian monk in April, 15, 18, and it's held in Heidelberg.
sentences.zh: 他是一位奥古斯丁修会的修士，会议在海德堡举行。

sentences.en: So it's quite a long way.
sentences.zh: 路程相当远。

sentences.en: Again, we see his mastery of publicity.
sentences.zh: 我们再次看到了他驾驭舆论的能力。

sentences.en: He walks there.
sentences.zh: 他是走着去的。

sentences.en: So that's really drawing attention to himself.
sentences.zh: 这确实引起了人们对他的关注。

sentences.en: And he's treated as an absolute celebrity everywhere he goes.
sentences.zh: 无论他走到哪里，他都被视为绝对的名人。

sentences.en: He's kind of cheered and he gets to Heidelberg and the local prince shows off his chapel and his castle and invites Luther to dine with him.
sentences.zh: 他受到欢呼，到达海德堡后，当地的王公向他展示了自己的礼拜堂和城堡，并邀请路德与他共进晚餐。

sentences.en: So it's all tremendous.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切都非常了不起。

sentences.en: So Tom, is there a slight Jordan Peterson side to all this?
sentences.zh: 那么汤姆，这一切是否有一点乔丹·彼得森的影子？

sentences.en: Yes, a little bit, I think.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想有一点。

sentences.en: A celebrity professor who has said the unsayable and who has suddenly, you know, do you remember how people first reported when Jordan Peterson was doing rallies and stuff?
sentences.zh: 一位说了不可言说之事的明星教授，突然间，你知道，你还记得乔丹·彼得森刚开始举行集会时人们是怎么报道的吗？

sentences.en: People would say, it's amazing that somebody who's basically talking about, what is it, something to do with lobsters?
sentences.zh: 人们会说，令人惊奇的是，有人竟然在谈论，是什么来着，关于龙虾之类的东西？

sentences.en: Jungian philosophy and stuff.
sentences.zh: 荣格哲学之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And Jungian philosophy is inspiring young people.
sentences.zh: 而荣格哲学正在激励年轻人。

sentences.en: You know, what a remarkable thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这真是件了不起的事。

sentences.en: And it's the same.
sentences.zh: 情况是一样的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全一样。

sentences.en: If you think that he is saying things that in universities for a long time have been unsayable, Luther is doing something similar at Heidelberg.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为他所说的话在大学里长期以来都是不可言说的，那么路德在海德堡所做的事情也类似。

sentences.en: So he is now directly attacking the foundations of the theology that has prevailed in the Latin West for centuries and centuries.
sentences.zh: 他现在正在直接攻击几个世纪以来在拉丁西方占主导地位的神学基础。

sentences.en: So as opposed to the idea that reason, as mediated through Aristotle, enables you to understand God,
sentences.zh: 与那种认为理性——通过亚里士多德作为中介——能让你理解上帝的观点相反，

sentences.en: Luther says that reason is actually a whore.
sentences.zh: 路德说理性实际上是个妓女。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He says that philosophy is a delusion, that the only true Christian is a fool.
sentences.zh: 他说哲学是一种妄想，真正的基督徒只能是个傻瓜。

sentences.en: He says out front, I believe it is impossible for the church to be reformed unless church law,
sentences.zh: 他直言不讳地说，我相信除非教会法——也就是教规，及其规则和法令，以及目前所教授的经院神学、哲学和逻辑学被根除并被其他研究取代，否则教会是不可能改革的。

sentences.en: so that's canon law, with its rules and decrees, scholastic theology, philosophy and logic, as they are now taught, are eradicated and replaced by other studies.
sentences.zh: 我每天都祈求上帝，让纯粹的圣经研究和教会先贤的研究能尽快回归。

sentences.en: Daily, I ask the Lord that the pure study of the Bible and the church fathers might be summoned back as soon as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像乔丹·彼得森说性别研究全是胡扯。

sentences.en: So that is a bit like Jordan Peterson saying, gender studies, it's all woo-woo.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，后殖民研究，全是无稽之谈。

sentences.en: You know, post-colonial studies, all nonsense.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这一切都抛弃吧。

sentences.en: Let's get rid of it all.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到研究莎士比亚之类的东西上去。

sentences.en: Let's go back to studying Shakespeare or whatever.
sentences.zh: 或者这就像那场特定辩论中另一方的人攻击他们自己的学科一样。

sentences.en: And just to put that into context, Tom, the difference between him and the people we're talking about in the modern world is he will die if he gets this wrong.

sentences.zh: 没错，所以才叫这个名字。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, his real name is Tommaso de Vio.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的真名是托马索·德·维奥。

sentences.en: And he names himself Tommaso after Thomas Aquinas, who is the greatest of the medieval theologians.
sentences.zh: 他以托马斯·阿奎那的名字命名自己为托马索，阿奎那是中世纪最伟大的神学家。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Devotee of Aristotle.
sentences.zh: 亚里士多德的忠实信徒。

sentences.en: And the guy that Luther hates.
sentences.zh: 也是路德所憎恨的人。

sentences.en: And the person who Luther particularly hates, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是路德特别憎恨的那个人。

sentences.en: But as well as being a churchman, he's also a very, very skillful diplomat, despite the fact that he goes around insulting the Spanish king.
sentences.zh: 但除了作为一名教会人士，他也是一位非常、非常高明的政治家，尽管他到处侮辱西班牙国王。

sentences.en: And so, he's been sent to Augsburg, not specifically to meet Luther, but to try and coordinate a
sentences.zh: 所以，他被派往奥格斯堡，并不是专门为了见路德，而是为了尝试协调一场

sentences.en: crusade against the Turks, who are starting to really move into the Balkans at this point.
sentences.zh: 针对土耳其人的十字军东征，当时土耳其人已经开始真正进入巴尔干半岛了。

sentences.en: So, this is fascinating, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以，这很迷人，不是吗？

sentences.en: So, we talked last time, didn't we, or a couple of episodes ago, about how the Ottomans had captured
sentences.zh: 我们上次，或者几集前谈到过奥斯曼帝国是如何在

sentences.en: Constantinople in 1453.
sentences.zh: 1453年攻占君士坦丁堡的。

sentences.en: An absolutely, unbelievably shocking moment for Christendom.
sentences.zh: 这对基督教世界来说是一个绝对、令人难以置信的震撼时刻。

sentences.en: So, they take Algiers in 1516.
sentences.zh: 他们在1516年占领了阿尔及尔。

sentences.en: They're sort of spreading through the Mediterranean.
sentences.zh: 他们正在地中海地区扩张。

sentences.en: But they're going to capture Belgrade in 1521.
sentences.zh: 但他们将在1521年攻占贝尔格莱德。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, they're preparing for a big campaign against Belgrade this very summer.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们就在今年夏天准备对贝尔格莱德发动大规模战役。

sentences.en: Then they crush Hungary five years later.
sentences.zh: 五年后，他们又粉碎了匈牙利。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then by the end of the 1520s, they are going to be at the gates of Vienna.
sentences.zh: 到1520年代末，他们将兵临维也纳城下。

sentences.en: So, really, within striking distance of Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以，真的已经到了德国的打击范围之内了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And remember that we talked about Johann Hilton, the monk in Eisenberg, where Luther was at school,
sentences.zh: 还记得我们谈到过约翰·希尔顿吗？就是路德上学时在艾森伯格的那位僧侣，

sentences.en: who, you know, he supposedly wrote prophecies in his own blood.
sentences.zh: 据说他曾用自己的血写下预言。

sentences.en: And he had prophesied that Germany would be conquered by the Turks and that this would herald the coming of the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: 他预言德国将被土耳其人征服，这将预示着世界末日的到来。

sentences.en: Now, Caetan is absolutely against this.
sentences.zh: 现在，卡耶坦完全反对这一点。

sentences.en: The papacy is not in favour of the idea that the apocalypse is threatening.
sentences.zh: 教皇并不赞同世界末日即将来临的观点。

sentences.en: And, in fact, in 1513, a council in the Lateran palace in Rome had specifically prohibited preaching the imminence of the AntichriSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，1513年罗马拉特兰宫的一次会议专门禁止宣扬敌基督即将降临。

sentences.en: But, of course, Luther is all over this, not least because Hilton, this prophetic monk, had foretold that a great prophet would emerge in 1516, which is close enough to 1517,
sentences.zh: 但当然，路德对此非常热衷，尤其是因为希尔顿这位预言僧侣曾预言一位伟大的先知将在1516年出现，这离1517年已经很近了，

sentences.en: for Luther to think that it might actually be him.
sentences.zh: 足以让路德认为那个人可能就是他自己。

sentences.en: And just on that apocalyptic thing, Tom, you and I know, and everyone listening to this knows, that the Ottomans didn't get into Central and Western Europe.
sentences.zh: 关于那个末日论，汤姆，你我都清楚，听众也都清楚，奥斯曼人并没有进入中欧和西欧。

sentences.en: Well, they didn't get beyond Hungary.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们没能越过匈牙利。

sentences.en: They didn't take Vienna.
sentences.zh: 他们没能攻下维也纳。

sentences.en: They didn't get into Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们没能进入德国。

sentences.en: But nobody knows that then.
sentences.zh: 但当时没人知道这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole Luther story surely only makes sense if you think that this is a society that thinks it is facing imminent invasion, occupation, the stamping out of Christianity,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整个路德的故事只有在你认为这是一个认为自己正面临迫在眉睫的入侵、占领、基督教被抹杀的社会时，才说得通，

sentences.en: whatever.
sentences.zh: 无论如何。

sentences.en: There's this incredible sense of existential dread that hangs over the whole story.
sentences.zh: 整个故事笼罩着一种难以置信的生存恐惧感。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this really ties Hilton's hands in dealing with Luther, because we mentioned that the
sentences.zh: 这确实束缚了卡耶坦处理路德问题的手脚，因为我们提到过

sentences.en: emperor Maximilian is fading, and he wants to ensure that his grandson, Charles, will succeed him as emperor.
sentences.zh: 马克西米利安皇帝正在衰老，他想确保他的孙子查理能继任皇帝。

sentences.en: And this obviously gives enormous power to Frederick, Luther's defender and protector as an elector.
sentences.zh: 这显然赋予了作为选帝侯的路德的捍卫者和保护者腓特烈巨大的权力。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because it's not a done deal that a Habsburg will succeed.
sentences.zh: 因为哈布斯堡家族能否继位并不是板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: It could be somebody else.
sentences.zh: 可能是其他人。

sentences.en: No, it's not a done deal.
sentences.zh: 不，这不是板上钉钉的事。

sentences.en: I think the key thing is that Charles wants to be elected unanimously, and Frederick is keeping his cards close to his chest and not saying who he is going to vote for.
sentences.zh: 我认为关键在于查理希望全票当选，而腓特烈对自己的意图守口如瓶，没有说他会投给谁。

sentences.en: And so that means that Caetan, if he's to get a kind of united front against the Turks, he can't afford to alienate Frederick.
sentences.zh: 这意味着卡耶坦如果想建立一个统一战线对抗土耳其人，他就不能得罪腓特烈。

sentences.en: And this is why Frederick is able to persuade Caetan to meet Luther in Augsburg rather than have him sent to Rome.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么腓特烈能够说服卡耶坦在奥格斯堡会见路德，而不是把他送到罗马。

sentences.en: Again, Luther is very, very lucky about this.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，路德在这方面非常、非常幸运。

sentences.en: So he's lucky, but of course, he also has this incredible ability to seize the limelight.
sentences.zh: 所以他很幸运，但当然，他也有这种令人难以置信的抢占风头的能力。

sentences.en: And so, again, he goes to Augsburg on foot, kind of playing the humble man of God, as opposed to the splendor and pomp of Caetan as a kind of prince of the church.
sentences.zh: 于是，他再次徒步前往奥格斯堡，扮演谦卑的上帝仆人，与作为教会王子的卡耶坦的辉煌和排场形成鲜明对比。

sentences.en: Caetan welcomes him very gently.
sentences.zh: 卡耶坦非常温和地欢迎了他。

sentences.en: He's kind of playing the part of a father, speaking to a son, trying to persuade him of the error of his ways.
sentences.zh: 他扮演着父亲的角色，对儿子说话，试图说服他改正错误。

sentences.en: But they have three meetings, and over the course of the meetings, Caetan loses it more and more.
sentences.zh: 但他们进行了三次会面，在会面过程中，卡耶坦越来越失控。

sentences.en: He gets more and more cross.
sentences.zh: 他变得越来越恼火。

sentences.en: His voice goes up higher and higher because he realizes very, very quickly that what's at stake is not the details of the 95 Theses.
sentences.zh: 他的声音越来越高，因为他很快意识到，危及的不是《九十五条论纲》的细节。

sentences.en: It's about, essentially, who has authority in the Christian world.
sentences.zh: 本质上，这是关于谁在基督教世界拥有权威的问题。

sentences.en: And to Caetan, it seems self-evident who does.
sentences.zh: 对卡耶坦来说，谁拥有权威是不言而喻的。

sentences.en: It's the church.
sentences.zh: 是教会。

sentences.en: It's the Catholic church.
sentences.zh: 是天主教会。

sentences.en: It always has done.
sentences.zh: 一直如此。

sentences.en: It always will.
sentences.zh: 永远如此。

sentences.en: I mean, to question that is just unspeakable.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，质疑这一点简直是不可理喻。

sentences.en: But Luther is questioning that.
sentences.zh: 但路德正在质疑这一点。

sentences.en: He's questioning the papacy.
sentences.zh: 他正在质疑教皇制度。

sentences.en: He's questioning canon law.
sentences.zh: 他正在质疑教会法。

sentences.en: He's questioning all the philosophy derived from Aristotle, all of it.
sentences.zh: 他正在质疑所有源自亚里士多德的哲学，全部质疑。

sentences.en: And Luther is arguing that all that really matters is the Bible, sola scriptura, scripture alone.
sentences.zh: 路德主张唯一重要的是圣经，即“唯独圣经”。

sentences.en: And he says to Caetan, the Pope is not above, but under the word of God.
sentences.zh: 他对卡耶坦说，教皇不在上帝的话语之上，而是在其之下。

sentences.en: And Caetan can't believe it.
sentences.zh: 卡耶坦简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: He can't believe that he is arguing with this obscure monk who is making this case and refusing to accept the majesty of the teachings of the church.
sentences.zh: 他不敢相信自己竟然在和一个默默无闻的僧侣争论，而这个僧侣提出了这种观点，并拒绝接受教会教义的威严。

sentences.en: So to use an analogy that you've used previously in the podcast, in the series, it is the equivalent
sentences.zh: 所以，用你在播客和系列节目中用过的类比，这相当于

sentences.en: of an incredibly distinguished scientist, one of the world's great scientists, suddenly finding that he's got to have a debate with somebody who not merely doesn't come anywhere
sentences.zh: 一位极其杰出的科学家，世界上最伟大的科学家之一，突然发现自己必须与一个不仅在地位上远不及他，

sentences.en: near him in eminence, but says, I don't really believe in your science, and is kind of ripping
sentences.zh: 而且说“我真的不相信你的科学”，并从基础上将其拆毁，说他不接受科学家及其同事认为理所当然的一切的人进行辩论。

sentences.en: it down to the foundations and saying he doesn't accept everything that the scientist and his colleagues take for granted.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: But I suppose the difference would be that this person who's opposing the professor would have a basic grounding that would enable him to argue his case, because Luther is
sentences.zh: 但我认为区别在于，这个反对教授的人会有基础知识，使他能够为自己的观点辩护，因为路德在说，

sentences.en: saying, you know, disprove me, go to the Bible and prove to me that the Pope should have this and that Aristotle is right on that or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道，反驳我吧，去查圣经，向我证明教皇应该拥有这个，亚里士多德在那个问题上是对的，或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And that's a problem for him, right?
sentences.zh: 这对他是问题，对吧？

sentences.en: That is a problem.
sentences.zh: 那确实是个问题。

sentences.en: And Caetan comes back and says, yes, but this is, you know, this is the majesty of the church.
sentences.zh: 卡耶坦回来后说，是的，但这是，你知道，这是教会的威严。

sentences.en: This is tradition.
sentences.zh: 这是传统。

sentences.en: I embody it.
sentences.zh: 我体现了它。

sentences.en: And Luther says, you know, my conscience is more important to me than what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 路德说，你知道，我的良心对我来说比你说的更重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And here he is making the plea for conscience, which again is so important to the way that I think people in the modern West understand the basis for what they do.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他为良心进行了辩护，这在我看来对于现代西方人理解他们行为的基础非常重要。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, their moral underpinnings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们的道德基础。

sentences.en: But again, it is Luther who is taking this step and foregrounding conscience as something that is more important than anything else, really.
sentences.zh: 但同样，是路德迈出了这一步，并将良心置于比任何其他事物都重要的位置，真的。

sentences.en: And so you can see why Caetan completely loses his rag and tells Luther to go away.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看出为什么卡耶坦完全发火了，并叫路德走开。

sentences.en: And so, you know, only come back if you're prepared to recant and Luther isn't.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，除非你准备忏悔，否则别回来，而路德没有。

sentences.en: And so what happens is that Staupitz, who is the head of the Augustinians in Germany, the
sentences.zh: 于是发生的事情是，德国奥古斯丁修会的负责人施陶皮茨，

sentences.en: guy who'd originally made Luther a professor at Wittenberg, he releases Luther from his vows.
sentences.zh: 那个最初让路德成为维滕贝格教授的人，他解除了路德的誓言。

sentences.en: And so that means he's no longer part of the Augustinians.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他不再是奥古斯丁修会的一员了。

sentences.en: And so Luther is now, you know, he feels he's alone, but to be alone for Luther is liberating.
sentences.zh: 所以路德现在，你知道，他感到自己孤身一人，但对路德来说，孤独是解放。

sentences.en: It brings you closer to God.
sentences.zh: 它让你更接近上帝。

sentences.en: And so he displays his love of God by writing two unbelievably rude letters, one that he sends to Caetan, one to the Pope.
sentences.zh: 于是他通过写两封极其粗鲁的信来表达他对上帝的爱，一封寄给卡耶坦，一封寄给教皇。

sentences.en: And then he clambers over the city walls of Augsburg and he scarpers back to Wittenberg.
sentences.zh: 然后他翻过奥格斯堡的城墙，溜回了维滕贝格。

sentences.en: So he's been kicked out of the Augustinians.
sentences.zh: 所以他被踢出了奥古斯丁修会。

sentences.en: Is that effectively what's happened?
sentences.zh: 这实际上就是发生的事情吗？

sentences.en: I think it's been a mutually agreed separation.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个双方同意的分离。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Because Staupitz thinks, I don't need this hassle.
sentences.zh: 因为施陶皮茨想，我不需要这种麻烦。

sentences.en: You know, this is embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这很尴尬。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want his order and himself personally to be dragged down into the kind of the magic mix of all this stuff that's going on.
sentences.zh: 他不希望他的修会和他个人被拖入所有这些正在发生的混乱之中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I think it would be best for the reputation of the order, Martin.
sentences.zh: 我想这对修会的声誉最好，马丁。

sentences.en: But, you know, already this kind of concern with what institutions will think is starting to look very retro because Luther, again, is broadcasting his perspective.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这种对机构会怎么想的担忧已经开始显得非常过时了，因为路德再次在广播他的观点。

sentences.en: And because it's more interesting, it gets far more attention.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它更有趣，所以得到了更多的关注。

sentences.en: So he gets back to Wittenberg and he writes up an account of his encounter with Caetan.
sentences.zh: 所以他回到维滕贝格，写了一份关于他与卡耶坦相遇的记录。

sentences.en: And it has pleased heaven that I should become the talk of the people.
sentences.zh: “上天乐见我成为人们谈论的话题。”

sentences.en: Nice.
sentences.zh: 不错。

sentences.en: Which is tremendous.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Humble bragging.
sentences.zh: 凡尔赛文学。

sentences.en: And of course, Caetan, he's not going to broadcast an account of what he did.
sentences.zh: 当然，卡耶坦是不会去广播他所做的事情的记录的。

sentences.en: So Luther is like someone who has masses of social media accounts.
sentences.zh: 所以路德就像一个拥有大量社交媒体账号的人。

sentences.en: And Caetan is like someone who doesn't even have an email address.
sentences.zh: 而卡耶坦就像一个连电子邮件地址都没有的人。

sentences.en: And it means that Luther can dominate the terms of the debate.
sentences.zh: 这意味着路德可以主导辩论的条款。

sentences.en: But you compared Luther to Jordan Peterson.
sentences.zh: 但你把路德比作乔丹·彼得森。

sentences.en: Of course, Jordan Peterson provokes massive counter-reaction.
sentences.zh: 当然，乔丹·彼得森引发了巨大的反弹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't have it all his own way.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他并没有一切都如愿以偿。

sentences.en: You know, he's endlessly being abused.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不断地受到辱骂。

sentences.en: And so the same thing starts to happen to Luther.
sentences.zh: 所以同样的事情也开始发生在路德身上。

sentences.en: That Luther is not the only person who is able to use the printing press.
sentences.zh: 路德并不是唯一能够使用印刷机的人。

sentences.en: There are other people as well.
sentences.zh: 还有其他人。

sentences.en: There are other people with a sense of occasion.
sentences.zh: 还有其他人有这种场合感。

sentences.en: And one of them is a former colleague, a friend of Luther's, a man called Johann Eck.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是路德的前同事，路德的朋友，一个叫约翰·埃克的人。

sentences.en: And Eck is appalled by where Luther is going and challenges him to a debate.
sentences.zh: 埃克对路德的走向感到震惊，并向他发起辩论挑战。

sentences.en: And again, this is very 21st century, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这非常有21世纪的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: This would happen now.
sentences.zh: 现在也会发生这种情况。

sentences.en: Richard Dawkins meeting with a bishop or appearing on the Joe Rogan show or something like that.
sentences.zh: 理查德·道金斯会见主教，或者出现在乔·罗根的节目上之类的。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是。

sentences.en: It's that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 就是那种事。

sentences.en: And Eck challenges Luther to a debate.
sentences.zh: 埃克向路德发起了辩论挑战。

sentences.en: Luther agrees and he'll go with Karlstadt, the chancellor of Wittenberg University, who's kind of rallying behind Luther.
sentences.zh: 路德同意了，他将与维滕贝格大学校长卡尔施塔特一起去，后者正在支持路德。

sentences.en: And actually ends up being more radical than Luther, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 实际上他最终比路德更激进，不是吗？

sentences.en: He gets so excited by Luther's message.
sentences.zh: 他被路德的信息弄得太兴奋了。

sentences.en: Yeah, he does.
sentences.zh: 没错，他确实这么做了。

sentences.en: He does.
sentences.zh: 他确实做了。

sentences.en: We'll come to that.
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会谈到这一点。

sentences.en: And Luther accepts the invitation to go to Leipzig, but this turns out to be a bad mistake.
